skill.name: video-extend
skill.description: Extend existing video clips with RunComfy by choosing a Veo 3-1 extend endpoint, writing a continuation prompt, and running the RunComfy CLI.
skill.summary: Continue short Veo clips with RunComfy using guided prompts and CLI commands.
skill.author: runcomfy-com

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced CLI examples, documentation links, and a disclosed CLI token storage note. The skill is a RunComfy workflow guide that sends user-approved video URLs and prompts to the RunComfy service; no prompt injection attempt, credential exfiltration, arbitrary shell execution, or hidden file abuse was found. Users should still treat video URLs, prompts, generated media, and API tokens as sensitive because the workflow depends on an external service.

remediation.suggestion: Keep telling users that source video URLs and prompts are sent to RunComfy, and use only media the user explicitly approved.
Keep documenting token storage permissions and recommend RUNCOMFY_TOKEN for CI without printing tokens in prompts or logs.
Keep shell examples limited to RunComfy CLI usage and avoid adding remote install scripts or arbitrary shell pipelines.

content.value_statement: Short generated clips often need more time, cleaner endings, or connected story beats. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code extend approved videos with RunComfy.
actual_capabilities: Selects Veo 3-1 Extend or Fast Extend based on quality, cost, and iteration needs.
Builds RunComfy CLI guidance with video URL, continuation prompt, and output directory parameters.
Explains continuation prompt patterns for camera motion, scene beats, and identity continuity.
Advises how to chain generated outputs into longer shot sequences.
Documents CLI setup, exit codes, endpoint choices, and related RunComfy skills.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI and a valid RunComfy account token.
Depends on external RunComfy and Google Veo model availability.
Does not create the initial source clip from scratch.
Long chains can accumulate identity drift or motion changes.

use_cases.title: Lengthen a Hero Clip
use_cases.description: Extend a short Veo clip into a longer presentation shot while preserving motion and lighting.

use_cases.title: Draft Multi-Beat Storyboards
use_cases.description: Chain short extensions into several narrative beats before selecting final takes.

use_cases.title: Prototype Campaign Variants
use_cases.description: Use Fast Extend to test continuation ideas before spending on final-quality output.

prompt_templates.title: Extend a Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one simple continuation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Extend this source video: [video URL]. Keep the camera steady and continue the current action for five seconds.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Quality Mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request that balances draft speed and final quality.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Fast Extend for draft versions of this clip: [video URL]. Create three continuation prompts with different camera movement.

prompt_templates.title: Chain Story Beats
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a longer sequence made from several extensions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three consecutive extensions for this clip: [video URL]. Keep each beat focused and describe how each output feeds the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Production Continuity Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced production review before running final output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a final-quality extension plan for this hero clip: [video URL]. Include endpoint choice, prompt wording, drift risks, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A user asks to make an eight-second product shot feel longer.
output: Recommended Veo 3-1 Extend for final quality.
Continuation prompt focuses on a slow camera push and steady product motion.
Review checklist covers lighting, identity, motion, and ending frame quality.

output_examples.input: A user wants several draft endings for a short scene.
output: Recommended Fast Extend for low-cost iteration.
Prepared three alternate continuation directions with one main beat each.
Suggested using the best draft as the input for a final-quality extension.

output_examples.input: A user wants a longer narrative from one seed clip.
output: Split the story into short extension beats.
Planned each continuation around camera direction and subject continuity.
Flagged identity drift as a review point after each generated clip.

best_practices: Use only source videos the user explicitly provided or approved.
Keep each continuation prompt to one main beat and clear camera direction.
Use Fast Extend for drafts, then full Extend for final-quality clips.
anti_patterns: Do not pass private or unlicensed video URLs to the external model.
Do not combine several action beats into one extension prompt.
Do not treat generated output as final without checking identity drift and unintended motion.

faq.question: What does this skill extend?
faq.answer: It extends an existing video clip by guiding RunComfy to generate the next segment.

faq.question: Does it create a source video from scratch?
faq.answer: No. Use an image-to-video or text-to-video workflow first, then use this skill to continue the result.

faq.question: Which model endpoint does it use?
faq.answer: It routes to Google Veo 3-1 Extend or Fast Extend through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Can it make long videos?
faq.answer: It can chain several short extensions, but each generation should stay focused to reduce drift.

faq.question: What should the prompt describe?
faq.answer: Describe what happens next, including camera direction and one main action beat.

faq.question: What privacy care is needed?
faq.answer: Use only approved video URLs and avoid sending private media or sensitive prompt details to the external service.
